The ether can be written as

\[
\mathrm{PhO{-}CH_2{-}C(CH_3)_2{-}CH{=}CH_2}.
\]

Under strongly acidic HBr conditions, the terminal alkene is protonated to give the internal carbocation:

\[
\mathrm{PhO{-}CH_2{-}C(CH_3)_2{-}CH^+{-}CH_3}.
\]

This carbocation has two intramolecular fates:

1. **Direct attack by an ortho carbon of the benzene ring** closes a six-membered ring. After rearomatization, this gives **3,3,4-trimethylchromane**.

2. A **1,2-methyl shift** first converts the secondary cation into the tertiary cation  
   \[
   \mathrm{PhO{-}CH_2{-}C^+(CH_3){-}CH(CH_3)_2}.
   \]
   Ortho attack now closes a five-membered ring, producing **3-isopropyl-3-methyl-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran**.

Thus, the two new TLC spots are consistent with the pair in option B.

Answer: B
